caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:v1v2-1
attempts.entry_title: V1 coordination before V2 spiking in anesthetized macaques (Zandvakili and Kohn 2015)
attempts.summary: The paper's central finding, that V1 population coordination is stronger just before spikes of middle-layer V2 neurons, held in this data, though the increase is about twofold against the paper's threefold and some elevation also appears after V2 spikes. Narrow V1-V2 cross-correlation peaks were far more common than the paper reports, which may come from the five deposited sessions or from this attempt's method. In these pairs V2 spikes lag V1 spikes by less than the paper's delay, a measure limited by the files' 1 ms spike times. The lack of coordination before spikes outside the middle layers could not be tested, as the data hold no recording depths, and the network simulations were not attempted.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Zandvakili and Kohn (2015) on CRCNS data set v1v2-1, which holds the spike times of V1 Utah array units and V2 tetrode units in 5 sessions from 3 anesthetized macaques viewing drifting gratings, with receptive field fits per channel. It computes the jitter-corrected V1-V2, V1-V1 and V2-V2 cross-correlograms, finds the V2 sites with a narrow V1-V2 peak, and measures the Jensen-Shannon divergence of V1 population states around V2 spikes against control epochs and shuffled data, under every reading of the open method details. The V2 depths, unit SNR and the pixel-to-degree scale that the layer, single-unit and receptive field analyses need are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Zandvakili and Kohn (2015) from CRCNS v1v2-1

outcomes.statement: V1-V2 CCGs frequently have broad peaks, tens to hundreds of milliseconds wide, evident in site-average CCGs at all laminar locations.
outcomes.source: Results, V1-V2 Recordings, paragraph 4 ("To understand how"); Figure 4C, left
outcomes.quote: We frequently observed broad peaks in V1-V2 CCGs, tens to hundreds of milliseconds wide. These were evident in the average V1-V2 CCGs at all laminar locations
outcomes.notes: All 31 site-average shuffle-corrected V1-V2 CCGs have a broad peak under both readings (mean over -50 to 50 ms above the flank mean, and above zero), 16 of 16 sites with a narrow peak and 15 of 15 without. The across-site average peaks at 2 ms and is 68 ms wide at half its height above the flank mean; it stays above half its height above zero over the whole +-125 ms.
deviations: A site is a V2 tetrode in one session; the files hold no depth, so "all laminar locations" is tested as sites with and without a narrow peak, as the criterion says.
Spike times are in 1 ms bins in the files; the paper used 0.1 ms.

outcomes.statement: A significant narrow peak in the site-average V1-V2 CCG occurs at a minority of V2 sites (46 of 223).
outcomes.source: Results, V1-V2 Recordings, paragraph 5 ("At a subset of V2 sites")
outcomes.quote: Average V1-V2 CCGs contained a significant narrow peak at 46 of 223 V2 sites
outcomes.notes: 16 of 31 V2 sites have a significant narrow peak in the site-average jitter-corrected CCG with the 10 ms jitter window (reading j-a), 0.516 against 0.206 +/- 0.021; 22 of 31 (0.710) with a 25 ms window. Per animal 3 of 6, 5 of 11 and 8 of 14. With a 4 or 6 SD threshold, 22 and 13 sites. The excess is in every session (2 of 5 to 5 of 7 sites), so no single session accounts for it. The data set holds 31 sites of the paper's 223 and 5 of its sessions; the paper says some penetrations targeted middle-layer sites, so the fraction may depend on which sessions were deposited, which the documentation does not say. It may also come from this attempt's method (1 ms bins, no SNR criterion, the jitter implementation). An excess in every session fits either cause, and without depths the two cannot be separated.
deviations: CCGs at 1 ms resolution (the files' resolution) against the paper's 0.1 ms. Equation 1 is combined over the eight stimuli by summing coincidences and the normaliser, which weights each stimulus by its V1 spike count (a standard choice).

The jitter correction subtracts the expected CCG under the jitter the claims file describes for the divergence analysis (each spike redrawn from the neuron's spikes in the same window on trials of the same stimulus), computed analytically for both neurons, with windows tiling the trial from 0 ms (Pairwise V1-V2 Analysis cites Smith and Kohn 2008 for the jitter). The 25 ms window is this attempt's choice for reading j-b, which the claims file leaves unnamed.
The SNR >= 2 unit criterion cannot be applied (no waveforms); units below 0.5 sp/s are removed.

outcomes.statement: V2 sites with a narrow V1-V2 CCG peak lie on average 694 um superficial to the layer 6/white matter border, the expected depth of layer 4 and deep layer 3.
outcomes.source: Results, V1-V2 Recordings, paragraph 5 ("At a subset of V2 sites")
outcomes.quote: whose mean depth was 694 ± 49 (SEM) microns superficial to the layer 6/white matter border
outcomes.notes: The files hold no recording depth for any V2 site and no layer 6/white matter reference; the descriptor lists spike rasters, stimulus codes, trial ids, unit codes and RF fits only.

outcomes.statement: The probability that a V1-V2 pair has a significant narrow CCG peak is highest for RF offsets below 0.5 deg, about 1%, and falls quickly with greater offset.
outcomes.source: Results, V1-V2 Recordings, paragraph 6 ("The probability of observing"); Figure 5A
outcomes.quote: The probability was highest for pairs with offsets of <0.5�, and decayed quickly with greater offsets (Figure 5A). Even for pairs with well-aligned RFs, the probability was only �1%
outcomes.notes: RF centres are in pixels and the data set gives no pixel-to-degree scale and no fixation point; the paper gives 1024 x 768 pixels at 110 cm without the screen size, so the 0.5 deg bins of the criterion cannot be formed. Shown for information only, in pixels and the first eye, the probability of a significant pair falls with RF offset (0.0165 at 0 to 25 px, 0.0136 at 25 to 50, 0.0106 at 50 to 75, 0.0034 at 75 to 100, 0 beyond 100 px; 15,463 pairs with both RFs fitted). The V1 rfInfo row of a unit is taken as its electrode code minus 1, and sessions with two eyes mapped use the first; 2 of 564 V1 units fall on a row with no fit, and the difference in probability between offsets below 50 px and 75 px or more (0.0121) is larger than under any of 200 random permutations of the V1 rows (median 0.0050, largest 0.0119), consistent with the mapping.

outcomes.statement: Only about 0.3% of all V1-V2 pairs have a significant narrow CCG peak (296 of 83,441).
outcomes.source: Results, V1-V2 Recordings, paragraph 6 ("The probability of observing")
outcomes.quote: In total, 0.3% of V1-V2 pairs had a significant narrow peak (n = 296 out of 83,441 pairs)
outcomes.notes: 171 of 16,308 V1-V2 pairs (0.0105) pass the 5 SD rule with 10 ms jitter, 185 (0.0113) with 25 ms, against 0.003 or 0.00355. Per session 0.0028 to 0.018; only 106r002p70 (6 of 2112, 0.0028) is within tolerance. Narrow peaks remain rare (about 1% of pairs). The site fraction of fig4c-narrow-peak-sites is 2.5 times the paper's, consistent with deposited sessions richer in coupled sites than the paper's sample or with a difference in method.
deviations: 1 ms bins against the paper's 0.1 ms; jitter as in fig4c-narrow-peak-sites.

outcomes.statement: Narrow V1-V2 CCG peaks are offset from zero lag by a median of 2.8 ms, significantly different from zero, with a mean peak width of 3.71 ms, consistent with direct V1 to V2 input.
outcomes.source: Results, V1-V2 Recordings, paragraph 7 ("We next analyzed"); Figure 5B, gray
outcomes.quote: Narrow peaks were offset from zero time lag by a median of 2.8 ms (Figure 5B, gray; p < 0.001 for difference with 0), with an average peak width of 3.71 ± 0.05 ms (SEM)

statistics.n: 296 V1-V2 pairs with a significant narrow peak

outcomes.notes: Of 171 significant V1-V2 pairs, 151 peak after zero lag, 5 at zero and 15 before; the offset differs from zero with p < 0.001 under both readings (Wilcoxon p = 7.1e-20, sign test p = 1.9e-29). The median offset is 2.0 ms, outside 2.8 +/- 0.28 (per animal 3, 2 and 2 ms). The peaks fall on whole milliseconds (23 at 1 ms, 55 at 2, 49 at 3, 18 at 4); a parabola through the peak bins, a variant not in the paper, gives a median of 2.30 ms, also outside. The mean width at half height is 3.89 +/- 0.07 ms on the smoothed CCG (reading a) and 3.09 +/- 0.09 ms unsmoothed (reading b), both outside 3.71 +/- 0.1. The criterion needs the test at p < 0.001 and the median within tolerance; the direction and significance of the offset hold, its size does not, so the outcome is not reproduced (changed from partially reproduced after the first verification round, as the criterion defines no partial outcome).
deviations: The files hold spike times in 1 ms bins, so offsets are whole milliseconds where the paper's were at 0.1 ms resolution; this limits both the median and the width. Smoothing a single 1 ms bin with the Gaussian of SD 1.5 ms alone gives a width at half height of 3.54 ms, so reading (a) has little room below that, and the unsmoothed width of reading (b) is limited by the bin.

outcomes.statement: Significant narrow peaks of V1-V1 and V2-V2 jitter-corrected CCGs have a median offset of 0.0 ms, not different from zero.
outcomes.source: Results, V1-V2 Recordings, paragraph 7 ("We next analyzed"); Figure 5B, blue and red
outcomes.quote: significant peaks in V1-V1 (Figure 5B; blue, n = 2845) and V2-V2 (red, n = 368) jitter-corrected CCGs had a median offset of 0.0 ms (p = 0.45 and 0.42, respectively, for difference from zero)
outcomes.notes: Both medians are 0.0 ms. V2-V2 (249 significant pairs of 2113) shows no difference from zero under either reading (Wilcoxon p = 0.861, sign test p = 0.703). V1-V1 (2620 of 32,770) differs under the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (p = 0.016 with zeros dropped, 0.027 Pratt, 0.028 zeros split) and not under the sign test (p = 0.076); mean offset 0.104 ms, 978 positive, 900 negative, 742 zero. The readings give different outcomes, and the outcome takes the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (see deviations), under which V1-V1 pairs differ from zero, so the criterion gives not reproduced. The outcome was not reproduced before the first verification round and partially reproduced after it, the outcome the verifier gave, on the ground that the two readings disagree. The second verifier pointed out that this does not follow from the assumed test; the change back to not reproduced was proposed and the third verification round agreed with it. The V1-V1 shift follows the order of the unit lists (the claims file's pair order), so it is an ordering asymmetry, not a lead of one population. Without pairs on the same electrode, V1-V1 gives Wilcoxon p = 0.009 and sign test p = 0.063, and V2-V2 (108 pairs; 141 of the 249 share a tetrode) Wilcoxon p = 0.030 and sign test p = 0.033; the claims file uses all pairs. Question for the authors, recorded as a finding; which test gave p = 0.45 and 0.42.
deviations: Assumed that the paper's test of a median offset against zero is the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (MATLAB signrank, documented as a test of zero median, the routine choice in a MATLAB-based analysis such as the data set's own scripts). The paper names no test; the sign test gives the opposite outcome for V1-V1 pairs.
The lag sign within an area follows the order of the unit lists, as the criterion says; 1 ms bins.

outcomes.statement: For significant V1-V2 pairs with peak offsets above 1 ms, the median efficacy (CCG integral within 2.5 ms of the peak) is 0.39%, mean 0.69%.
outcomes.source: Figure S3A; Supplemental Figure 3 text, Amplitude
outcomes.quote: In the analyzed pairs, the median efficacy was 0.39% (Figure S3A, mean 0.69 ± 0.06%)
outcomes.notes: 128 of 171 significant pairs have an offset above 1 ms, which at 1 ms resolution means 2 ms or more (255 in the paper). Reading a, jitter-corrected CCG, median 0.324% and mean 0.496 +/- 0.046%, below 0.39 +/- 0.039 and 0.69 +/- 0.12. Reading b, the raw CCG, gives median 6.494% and mean 9.479% uncorrected and median 0.820% and mean 1.268% shuffle-corrected, far above. Reading a per animal, median 0.334%, 0.559% and 0.258% (20, 31 and 77 pairs).
deviations: The integral within 2.5 ms of the peak is the sum of the five 1 ms bins centred on the peak lag (-2.5 to +2.5 ms at the files' resolution).

outcomes.statement: In epochs 1.5 to 3.5 ms before spikes of middle-layer V2 neurons, V1 divergence is significantly higher than in control epochs at every jitter window from 5 to 1280 ms.
outcomes.source: Results, V2 Spiking Is Preceded by Stronger V1 Coordination, paragraphs 2 and 3; Figure 6A
outcomes.quote: The divergence values in control epochs (blue) were significantly smaller than in epochs preceding V2 spiking (red; p = 0.011 for jitter window of 5 ms; p < 0.001 for all other jitter windows)
outcomes.notes: 88 V2 neurons at the 16 middle-layer sites (1,985,591 spikes from 50 ms; the paper 226 neurons). Main reading (e-a, s-a, r-a, d-a) at 5, 10, 20, 40, 80 and 1280 ms, spike against control divergence 4.05e-4 against 2.36e-4 bits at 5 ms up to 5.16e-3 against 2.12e-3 at 1280 ms, ratios 1.72 to 2.43, p < 0.001 at every window under p-a (no draw of 5000) and p-b (at most 0.00037). All other readings (s-b, r-b with three realizations, d-b, and single bins at 2 or 3 ms for e-b) give 6 of 6 windows. Per animal the ratio is 1.50 to 2.66.
deviations: Reading e-b, one 1 ms bin centred 2.5 ms before the spike, cannot be formed from 1 ms data; it is run as the bins centred 2 ms and 3 ms before, which bracket it.

The V2 spikes and the V1 states are both in 1 ms bins, so the epoch of the bins 2 and 3 ms before the spike covers V1 activity from about 1 to 4 ms before it, wider than the paper's 1.5 to 3.5 ms; this may dilute the spike-epoch divergence and lower the spike to control ratio (fig7a-threefold). Forced by the data.
The jitter pool includes the spike's own trial (the claims file says other trials), a standard choice; one trial in 400 changes the pool little. Epochs falling before 50 ms are dropped.
Middle-layer sites are those of fig4c-narrow-peak-sites, 16 of 31, a larger share than the paper's.

outcomes.statement: For jitter windows of 5 to 80 ms, divergence before middle-layer V2 spikes is roughly 3-fold that of control epochs.
outcomes.source: Results, V2 Spiking Is Preceded by Stronger V1 Coordination, paragraph 4 ("For epochs 1.5-3.5 ms before"); Figure 7A
outcomes.quote: Divergence values for epochs associated with V2 spiking were roughly 3-fold greater than in control epochs
outcomes.notes: Divergence before V2 spikes is about twice control, not three times. Main reading, ratios at 5 to 80 ms 1.716, 1.875, 1.923, 1.964 and 2.072; (a) geometric mean 1.906, (b) median 1.923, (c) 1 of 5 windows within 2 to 4. The s-b, r-b and d-b readings give geometric means of 1.837 to 1.903, medians of 1.836 to 1.927 and 0 or 1 of 5 windows in range. Reading e-b cannot be formed; of the single bins that bracket it, the bin 3 ms before gives a median of 2.011 and 3 of 5 windows in range, and the bin 2 ms before a median of 1.803 and 0 of 5. Only the first, a stand-in for one side of reading e-b, reaches the edge of the tolerance, under the median summary alone. The ratio is about 1.9, outside 3 +/- 1, so the outcome is not reproduced (changed from partially reproduced after the first verification round: the claim is the size of the effect, which fig6a-coordination-before-v2 tests the presence of, and the criterion defines no partial outcome).
deviations: Reading e-b approximated by single bins 2 and 3 ms before the spike, as in fig6a-coordination-before-v2.
The 1 ms binning widens the spike epoch to about 1 to 4 ms before the spike (see fig6a-coordination-before-v2), which may lower the ratio.

outcomes.statement: Divergence both before middle-layer V2 spikes and in control epochs is significantly larger than divergence of shuffled data, so V1 activity is coordinated also in control epochs.
outcomes.source: Results, V2 Spiking Is Preceded by Stronger V1 Coordination, paragraph 4 ("For epochs 1.5-3.5 ms before"); Figure 7A, black
outcomes.quote: Note that both for epochs preceding V2 spiking and for control epochs, the divergence values were significantly larger than those obtained from shuffled data (Figure 7A, black)
outcomes.notes: Under all four readings (trials shuffled within orientation or across all trials; spike or control epochs) and at every window from 5 to 80 ms, the shuffled divergence (1.82e-4 to 4.62e-4 bits) is below the lower 95% bootstrap bound of both the spike divergence (3.30e-4 to 1.36e-3) and the control divergence (2.01e-4 to 6.81e-4). The margin is thin at 5 ms with trials shuffled within orientation. Over five shuffle realizations the shuffled value there has mean 1.935e-4 (spike epochs) and 1.928e-4 (control epochs), SD about 1e-5, against a control bound of 2.013e-4, and in each of these two readings one realization of five is above the bound (2.073e-4 and 2.038e-4), which would leave 4 of 5 windows. At every other window and reading all five realizations are below both bounds. The outcome rests on the first realization, as the criterion compares one shuffled value; the mean of the five also gives 5 of 5 windows.
deviations: The shuffled value is one realization per reading, compared as a point value with the bootstrap bounds, as the criterion says; four more realizations show its spread. The shuffled data are jittered with the same rule as the data.

outcomes.statement: In epochs 1.5 to 3.5 ms after middle-layer V2 spikes, V1 divergence does not differ from control epochs for jitter windows of 5 to 80 ms.
outcomes.source: Results, V2 Spiking Is Preceded by Stronger V1 Coordination, paragraph 3 (from "In epochs 1.5-3.5 ms after"); Figure 6B
outcomes.quote: In epochs 1.5–3.5 ms after the occurrence of a V2 spike, there was no difference in divergence with control epochs, for jitter windows between 5 and 80 ms (Figure 6B; p > 0.18 for all comparisons)
outcomes.notes: In epochs 1.5 to 3.5 ms after V2 spikes the divergence is above control at 80 ms under both bootstrap readings in every reading of the method (main ratio 1.37, p-a no draw of 5000, p-b 0.0038; p-b 0.046 or less in the others), and at 40 ms under p-a (main ratio 1.20, p-b 0.099). Under the main reading the ratios at 5 to 20 ms are 1.03 to 1.08 (p-a 0.10 to 0.48). The elevation after the spike is smaller than before it (1.20 and 1.37 at 40 and 80 ms, against 1.96 and 2.07 before). In the other readings the ratios at 5 to 20 ms range from 0.959 (s-b, 10 ms) to 1.12 (d-b, 20 ms, p-a = 0.024). A null check compares two independent sets of control epochs. p-a gives p < 0.05 at 1 of 12 window and epoch combinations and at 13 of 150 time-course epochs (about 7.5 expected, binomial tail P = 0.039 if the epochs were independent, which they are not), so it runs somewhat above its nominal rate at 0.05; it gives no Bonferroni-significant epoch. p-b gives p < 0.05 at none and is conservative. The main after-spike differences at 40 and 80 ms (1.2e-4 and 2.7e-4 bits) are well above the largest control-against-control difference (4.5e-5 and 5.2e-5 bits), so they are not an artefact of the test. p-b alone decides the outcome at 80 ms.

outcomes.statement: At a jitter window of 1280 ms, V1 divergence is elevated both before and after middle-layer V2 spikes.
outcomes.source: Results, V2 Spiking Is Preceded by Stronger V1 Coordination, paragraph 3 (from "In epochs 1.5-3.5 ms after"); Figure 6A and 6B, bottom rows
outcomes.quote: For larger jitter windows, there was enhanced divergence both before and after V2 spiking, as illustrated for a jitter window of 1280 ms (red compared to blue; bottom row of Figures 6A and 6B; p < 0.001 for both cases)
outcomes.notes: At 1280 ms the divergence is above control before V2 spikes (5.16e-3 against 2.12e-3 bits, ratio 2.43) and after them (4.13e-3 against 2.07e-3, ratio 2.00), p < 0.001 under both bootstrap readings and in every reading of the method.

outcomes.statement: Enhanced V1 coordination is evident several milliseconds before middle-layer V2 spikes, but not in more distant epochs or after V2 spikes.
outcomes.source: Results, V2 Spiking Is Preceded by Stronger V1 Coordination, paragraph 5 ("We next determined"); Figure 7D
outcomes.quote: Enhanced V1 coordination was evident several milliseconds before V2 spiking, but not in more temporally distant epochs or in epochs following V2 activity
outcomes.notes: Under the main, s-b, r-b and d-b readings of the method and both offset readings, the largest spike minus control difference at each of the five windows is 2.5 to 3.5 ms before the V2 spike (main: the epoch centred 2.5 ms before in reading a, 2 ms epochs; the bin 3 ms before in reading b). Epochs wholly after the spike or more than 8 ms before it are also significant after Bonferroni correction over the 31 offsets. With the paired bootstrap (p-a) this holds at every window in every reading (main reading a, 10 to 19 epochs per window). With the independent bootstrap (p-b) it holds at 80 ms in the main, s-b and r-b readings (4 to 6 epochs; main reading a, 1.5, 6.5, 7.5, 8.5 and 9.5 ms after) and at 40 and 80 ms in d-b. A null check of two independent control sets finds no Bonferroni-significant epoch under either p reading and p < 0.05 at 13 of 150 epochs under p-a (about 7.5 expected; 5 of 30 at the 5 ms window) and 0 under p-b, so p-a runs somewhat above its nominal rate at 0.05 but not at the Bonferroni threshold. At 80 ms the difference is 8.3e-4 bits 2.5 ms before the spike and 2.7e-4 bits 2.5 ms after.
deviations: 2000 bootstrap draws per offset, a standard choice: the smallest p they give, 1/2000, is below the Bonferroni threshold 0.05/31, and 5000 draws for the 1240 comparisons of each reading would not fit the notebook's time. Offsets beyond 15 ms are not run; epochs falling before 50 ms are dropped.

An epoch counts as after the spike when it lies wholly after it (centre -1 ms or less); the epochs that hold the bin simultaneous with the spike (centre -0.5 ms for 2 ms epochs, 0 for 1 ms bins) are counted apart. Before the first verification round the 2 ms epoch at -0.5 ms counted as after; the outcome does not change.

outcomes.statement: Before spikes of V2 neurons in layers superficial or deep to the middle layers, V1 divergence does not differ from control epochs, apart from the 80 ms jitter window.
outcomes.source: Results, V2 Spiking Is Preceded by Stronger V1 Coordination, paragraph 6 ("If coordinated V1 epochs"); Figure 7B
outcomes.quote: In epochs 1.5–3.5 ms before V2 spikes in these layers, divergence was not significantly different from that measured in control epochs (Figure 7B; p = 0.008 for jitter window of 80 ms; p > 0.15 for other windows)
outcomes.notes: Needs V2 sites superficial or deep to the middle-layer sites of the same penetration. Each session holds one recording per V2 tetrode, with no depth and no penetration identity, so the order of sites cannot be known. Using sites without a narrow peak would not be the claim's group.

outcomes.statement: Across temporal offsets around non-middle-layer V2 spikes, the difference in V1 divergence from control is minimal.
outcomes.source: Results, V2 Spiking Is Preceded by Stronger V1 Coordination, paragraph 6 ("If coordinated V1 epochs"); Figure 7E
outcomes.quote: We explored a range of temporal offsets relative to the V2 spikes, but the difference in divergence between epochs around the time of V2 spikes and control epochs was minimal (Figure 7E)
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig7b-nonmiddle-no-coordination, blocked for lack of V2 depths and penetrations.

outcomes.statement: Before spikes of V2 neurons at middle-layer depths whose RFs are offset by at least 3 deg from the V1 population, V1 divergence does not differ from control.
outcomes.source: Results, V2 Spiking Is Preceded by Stronger V1 Coordination, paragraph 7 ("Finally, we wished"); Figure 7C and 7F
outcomes.quote: We found no difference in divergence in epochs associated with spiking of these V2 neurons, compared to control epochs (Figures 7C and 7F; p > 0.2 for all comparisons)
outcomes.notes: Needs V2 neurons 500 to 1000 um from the layer 6/white matter border, and RF offsets in degrees. The files hold no depth, and RF positions are in pixels with no scale (metadata_insufficient, as for fig5a-rf-alignment).

outcomes.statement: Using only well-isolated V2 single units (SNR of 3 or more) in the middle layers, divergence is still elevated before V2 spikes for most jitter windows.
outcomes.source: Figure S2A; Supplemental Figure 2 text, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: divergence was significantly elevated in epochs preceding V2 spiking, relative to control epochs, for most jitter windows (p=0.3 for 5 ms jitter window; p=0.08 for 10 ms; p<0.01 for all other comparisons)
outcomes.notes: Needs each unit's SNR (waveform amplitude over noise SD). The files hold no waveforms or SNR; each file's neuralData has only spikeRasters, stim, trialId, unitCodes and rfInfo. The sort codes in unitCodes (1 to 4 for V1, 1 to 13 for V2) number the units of an electrode and do not mark single units; the data description says the units mix single units and multiunit activity.

outcomes.statement: Using only V1 single units (SNR of 3 or more), V1 divergence is elevated before middle-layer V2 spikes at every jitter window, and not before non-middle-layer or offset-RF V2 spikes.
outcomes.source: Figure S2B; Supplemental Figure 2 text, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Divergence is elevated in a population of V1 single units before spiking in the middle layers of V2 (p<0.001 for all jitter windows). V1 divergence is not elevated before spiking in the superficial or deep layers of V2, or before spiking at offset V2 sites
outcomes.notes: Needs V1 unit SNR, which the files do not hold; it also depends on fig7b and fig7c, blocked for lack of depths.

outcomes.statement: V1 coordination is elevated before spikes of middle-layer V2 neurons both with and without a significant CCG peak with a recorded V1 neuron, slightly more for those with one.
outcomes.source: Figure S4; Supplemental Figure 4 text, paragraph 3; Results, Dissociation of Divergence Analysis, paragraph 4 ("In the final scenario")
outcomes.quote: Figure S4 shows that coordination in V1 was elevated in epochs preceding either subset of V2 cells, evident as higher divergence values associated with V2 spiking than in the corresponding control epochs. The increase in divergence was slightly stronger, when based on V2 neurons with a V1 partner
outcomes.notes: 39 middle-layer V2 neurons have a significant pair with a recorded V1 unit and 49 have none (73 and 153 in the paper). Under the main reading both subsets have spike divergence above control at 5 of 5 windows from 5 to 80 ms under p-a, and under p-b at 5 of 5 with a partner and 4 of 5 without (5 ms p = 0.150). Across the six readings of the shared method, the subset with a partner is above control at 5 of 5 windows under both p readings, and the subset without at 4 or 5 of 5 under p-a and 2 to 5 of 5 under p-b. One combination does not meet the criterion: e-b2 (the single bin 2 ms before, a stand-in for one side of reading e-b) with p-b, where the subset without a partner is above control at 2 of 5 windows. The outcome holds under the other readings, and the criterion takes any reading. The spike to control ratio is larger with a partner at all five windows in every reading (main 1.91 to 2.30 against 1.32 to 1.67).

outcomes.statement: V2 middle-layer divergence is higher before spikes in superficial and deep V2 layers than in control epochs for jitter windows above 10 ms, and also higher after them.
outcomes.source: Figure S5A and S5B; Supplemental Figure 5 text, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: The elevation in divergence was significant for all jitter windows greater than 10 ms (p=0.02 for jitter window of 20 ms; p=0.009 for 40 ms; p<0.001 for 80 ms)

statistics.about: before superficial or deep spikes, 20 ms window

outcomes.notes: Needs spikes of V2 units in layers superficial or deep to the middle layers, which cannot be identified without depths (fig7b-nonmiddle-no-coordination). Within a session the V2 units are from one depth per tetrode.

outcomes.statement: In a ten-layer feedforward network of integrate-and-fire neurons, spike packets propagate to the deepest layer with high convergence but not with low convergence, where downstream spiking beyond layers 2 or 3 is not associated with heightened layer 1 divergence.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraph 2 ("In the first FFN variant") and the paragraph beginning "When applied to the FFNs of Figure 1"; Figure 1A and 1B
outcomes.quote: Thus, beyond layers 2 or 3, downstream spiking is not associated with heightened coordination in layer 1, indicating a failure of spike packets to propagate
outcomes.notes: Not attempted. A simulation (data elsewhere), with no published code; the claims file gives a rerun criterion from the Supplemental Experimental Procedures, and nothing but the time this attempt spent on the claims on the data set kept it from being run. Recorded as not_runnable before the first verification round, which is not the reason, since nothing was tried.
outcomes.where: none deposited; a simulation, and the paper links no simulation code

outcomes.statement: In synthetic populations of 100 neurons, divergence rises about 3-fold when pairwise correlation goes from 0.1 to 0.2 and falls 3-fold from 0.1 to 0.05, and is insensitive to firing rate.

outcomes.notes: RF variances are in pixels with no pixel-to-degree scale in the data set or the paper. In pixels, the mean diameter (4 SD) is 60.9 px for 431 V1 channels and 119.9 px for 77 V2 channels (reading a; 60.4 and 118.9 under reading b). The ratio of V2 to V1 diameter, which needs no scale, is 1.97 against 2.27 / 1.21 = 1.88 in the paper. A scale of 50 to 53 px/deg would match both means, but nothing in the data set or the paper fixes it.

findings.statement: The data set holds no V2 recording depth, penetration identity, unit SNR or waveforms. The paper's layer groups (middle, superficial and deep V2), its depth of the narrow-peak sites, its offset-RF group and its single-unit analyses cannot be repeated; 7 of the paper's claims on the recordings are blocked for this.

Receptive field centres and variances (rfInfo) are in pixels, and neither the data set nor the paper gives the pixel-to-degree scale or the fixation point (the paper gives 1024 x 768 pixels at 110 cm without the screen size). In four sessions each channel has fits for two eyes, with V1 RF centres a median of 244 to 266 pixels apart horizontally. RF sizes and offsets in degrees, which the paper reports, cannot be computed.

The data set holds 5 sessions in 3 animals of the paper's recordings in 7 animals (31 V2 sites of 223). Its documentation does not say how they were chosen. This attempt finds a significant narrow V1-V2 peak at 16 of 31 sites (0.52, against 46 of 223 in the paper) and in 1.05% of V1-V2 pairs (against 0.3%), in every session. The difference may come from which sessions were deposited or from this attempt's method (1 ms bins, no SNR criterion, the jitter implementation); the data cannot separate the two.
The data description gives an average of 112.2 V1 units per session; the five files hold 159, 109, 88, 97 and 111 V1 units, an average of 112.8. The V2 average (29.4) matches.

The data description lists stimulus code 7 as a 135 deg grating, but the sessions description gives 180 deg for session 105l001p16. The population responses agree with the sessions description (code 7 correlates 0.911 with code 1, against 0.637 and 0.845 with codes 6 and 8). The spike rasters are at 1 ms resolution, where the paper's CCGs used 0.1 ms; the description does not say that the spike times were binned.

verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The executed notebook of the first run with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier tested the helper functions on synthetic inputs (CCG lag sign, jitter expectation, jitter_events, control_trials, js_bits, pop_counts, half_width, both bootstrap p functions under the null, the Equation 1 normalisation) and read the text outputs, not the figures. It had no attempt record. It reported no place where the claims file misreads the paper, so no question was added for a reader. Report in transcripts/zandvakili-2015/verifier-1-report.md. Its outcomes disagree with the record on three claims (fig5b-v1v2-latency, fig5b-intra-areal-zero-lag, fig7a-threefold), and the record now gives its outcomes on all three. Its general points were answered as follows. Point 9 (the jitter pool includes the spike's own trial) is stated in the notebook and the record, unchanged. Point 11 (site and pair fractions 2.5 to 3.5 times the paper's) is now shown per session, where the excess is in every session; with no depths it cannot be examined further. Its request to show that the files hold no further fields is met in the data check (only spikeRasters, stim, trialId, unitCodes and rfInfo; the sort codes number units per electrode). Its rendered figures were not reviewed by it, and nothing was changed for that.

disagreements.reason: The offset is positive and significant (Wilcoxon p = 7e-20, sign test p = 2e-29), but the median is 2.0 ms (2.30 interpolated) against 2.8 +/- 0.28. The width is 3.89 ms smoothed and 3.09 ms unsmoothed, both outside 3.71 +/- 0.1. The criterion needs the median within tolerance. Point 5, smoothing a single bin alone gives a FWHM of 3.54 ms, so the width test has little room, and the unsmoothed width is limited by the bin size.

Both medians are 0.0 ms. V2-V2 shows no difference under either test (p = 0.86 and 0.70). V1-V1 differs under the Wilcoxon reading (p = 0.016) but not under the sign test (p = 0.076), so only reading (b) matches. Point 3, the V1-V1 Wilcoxon result depends on the claims file's pair order (unit-list order); the mean offset is 0.10 ms, so this is an ordering asymmetry, not a lead. Also, 141 of the 249 significant V2-V2 pairs share a tetrode, and excluding them makes V2-V2 significant under both tests (p = 0.030 and 0.033).

The ratios are 1.56 to 2.14. Geometric means are 1.79 to 2.00 and medians 1.80 to 2.01. Reading (c) puts at most 3 of 5 windows in range. Only e-b3 with the median summary (2.011) reaches the edge of the 2 to 4 range.

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of the revised run, with its conclusion cells and summary, the helper module, the claims file, the attempt record and the paper. The verifier checked every result sentence, the summary and the record's notes against the printed outputs, and the status of each round-1 point. It did not review the rendered figures. It found no new place where the claims file misreads the paper, so no question was added for a reader. Report in transcripts/zandvakili-2015/verifier-2-report.md. Its general points were answered as follows. The selection finding and the summary claimed that the deposited sessions cause the excess of narrow-peak sites; they now say it may come from the sessions or from this attempt's method, and that the data cannot separate the two. The wording that the paired bootstrap is near its nominal level is replaced throughout (notebook, notes, bootstrap finding): the null check now prints the binomial tail (P = 0.039 for 13 of 150, 0.016 for 5 of 30 at 5 ms), and the after-spike results are supported by the largest null difference, as the verifier suggested. The README's row of non-middle-layer and related claims now says six, and the run time is corrected. The rendered figures were not reviewed, and nothing was changed for that.

paper_notes.statement: Question for the authors. Which test gave the p-values for the median CCG peak offsets against zero (p < 0.001 for V1-V2; p = 0.45 and 0.42 for V1-V1 and V2-V2)? On this data set the Wilcoxon signed-rank test finds the V1-V1 offsets different from zero (p = 0.016, mean 0.10 ms) and the sign test does not (p = 0.076); the attempt assumed the signed-rank test.

Question for the authors. How were the bootstrap p-values comparing divergence in spike and control epochs computed, with the same resampled neurons for both (paired) or from the two bootstrap distributions taken as independent? The paired reading finds after-spike epochs and epochs far from the spike above control at many offsets (Figure 7D) where the independent one finds them at the 80 ms window (and 40 ms in one reading). Comparing two independent control sets on this data set, the paired reading runs somewhat above its nominal rate (13 of 150 epochs at p < 0.05, about 7.5 expected; none at the Bonferroni threshold) and the independent one is conservative (0 of 150). The outcomes here are the same under both.

Question for the authors. The CCG jitter window used for the significance of narrow peaks is given only for Figure 4C (10 ms); was it the same for all pairs and sites? With 25 ms, 22 of 31 sites and 185 pairs pass on this data set, against 16 and 171 with 10 ms.

entries.name: zandvakili-2015
entries.title: V1 coordination before V2 spiking in anesthetized macaques (Zandvakili and Kohn 2015)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Zandvakili and Kohn (2015) on CRCNS data set v1v2-1, which holds the spike times of V1 Utah array units and V2 tetrode units in 5 sessions from 3 anesthetized macaques viewing drifting gratings, with receptive field fits per channel. It computes the jitter-corrected V1-V2, V1-V1 and V2-V2 cross-correlograms, finds the V2 sites with a narrow V1-V2 peak, and measures the Jensen-Shannon divergence of V1 population states around V2 spikes against control epochs and shuffled data, under every reading of the open method details. The V2 depths, unit SNR and the pixel-to-degree scale that the layer, single-unit and receptive field analyses need are not in the data set.
